record.projectDescription: Varied short Japanese speaking prompts, grammar guides, sentence flashcards, comprehension reveals and dialogues from live practice.

parts.text: Build complete Japanese sentences from English prompts, then use reveals to check meaning. Grammar and vocabulary support the speaking practice. Based on our November 13 live Japanese practice, with corrected explanations; not a record of mastery.
Start with the two meanings of と, noun + だと, linking actions with て, and 〜たあとで. Other pages explain feelings, apologies, wishes, obligations and possibilities.
Quick reference for verbs and everyday phrases from our speaking practice. Japanese examples use kanji and hiragana readings without romaji.
Full-sentence English-to-Japanese flashcards, grouped by sentence pattern. Read the prompt, say the whole Japanese sentence, then flip. Hiragana readings accompany the answer.
Read a Japanese sentence, work out its meaning and grammar, and reveal the answer. The examples are deliberately varied.
Short English-to-Japanese prompts, one at a time. Ask for a single-word hint if necessary; avoid giving away whole answers. Keep spoken Japanese slow, and don't repeatedly ask whether to stop.

と has two common jobs here.

1. WHEN / IF → a usual, predictable result.
雨が降ると、家にいます。（あめがふると、いえにいます。） — When it rains, I stay home.
コーヒーを飲むと、いい気分になります。（こーひーをのむと、いいきぶんになります。） — When I drink coffee, I feel good.
Attach と directly to the plain verb (降ると, 飲むと), not to the polite ます-form. For a one-off future plan, 〜たら is usually more natural: 家に帰ったら、電話します — When I get home, I'll call.

2. THAT → content of a thought or something learnt.
彼女は看護師だと思います。（かのじょはかんごしだとおもいます。） — I think she's a nurse.
難しいと思います。（むずかしいとおもいます。） — I think it's difficult.

Noun or な-adjective + だと: 看護師だと, 先生だと, 簡単だと. An い-adjective or plain verb needs no だ: 難しいと思う, 来ると思う. Here と means 'that', not 'when'.

Same spoken と, different structure. Pay attention to the meaning of what comes after と: a consequence versus 思う / 知る / 言う.

TWO JOBS OF と

WHEN / IF — typical result
[雨が 降る] ── と ──▶ [家に います]
‘When it rains, I stay home.’

QUOTED STATEMENT — what I think
[彼女は 看護師だ] ── と ──▶ [思います]
‘I think she is a nurse.’

NOUN + だ + と + 思う
い-ADJECTIVE + と + 思う
VERB (plain) + と + 思う

Say the full Japanese sentence from the English before turning each card over. The answer shows kanji plus a complete hiragana reading. The conditional と describes a natural/habitual result. Cards are reusable practice examples, not a record of achievement.

parts.text:
1. て-form links actions: 日曜日は映画を見て、のんびりします。（にちようびはえいがをみて、のんびりします。） — On Sundays, I watch a film and relax. 見る→見て.

2. 〜たあとで makes the order explicit: 食べたあとで、お茶を飲みます。（たべたあとで、おちゃをのみます。） — After eating, I drink tea. 食べる→食べた; 行く→行った; 終わる→終わった.

3. 〜と describes a habitual/natural result: コーヒーを飲むと、元気になります。（こーひーをのむと、げんきになります。） — Whenever I drink coffee, I feel energised.

Compare: 寝る前に本を読みます。 — I read before bed. 寝ると本を読みます means 'when I go to bed, I read', not 'before bed'. For a future decision use 〜たら: 家に帰ったら、電話します。 — When I get home, I'll call.

CHOOSING THE LINK

[手を 洗って] ─────→ [ご飯を 食べます]
'I wash my hands and eat.' (linked actions)

[食べた] ── あとで ──▶ [お茶を 飲みます]
'After eating, I drink tea.' (completion first)

[コーヒーを 飲む] ── と ──▶ [元気に なります]
'Whenever I drink coffee, I feel energised.' (typical result)

[帰った] ── たら ──▶ [電話します]
'When I get home, I'll call.' (specific future plan)

sections.title: How feelings change with なる

parts.text:
なる = to become. The form depends on what comes before it.

Noun / な-adjective phrase + に + なる:
いい気分になります。（いいきぶんになります。） — I get into a good mood.
元気になります。（げんきになります。） — I feel better / energetic.

い-adjective → く + なる:
うれしい → うれしくなります — I become happy.
悲しい → 悲しくなります（かなしくなります） — I become sad.
痛い → 痛くなります（いたくなります） — It begins to hurt.

ロックを聴くと、いい気分になります。 — Listening to rock puts me in a good mood.
ロックを聴くと、気分が明るくなります。 — Listening to rock brightens my mood. Both natural, slightly different descriptions.

Avoid 運動はいい気分になります (exercise itself does not acquire a mood). Say 運動すると、いい気分になります — When I exercise, I feel good.

HOW TO SAY 'BECOMES'

[いい 気分] + に + なります
           noun phrase
            ↓
'I get into a good mood'

[元気] + に + なります
   な-adjective
            ↓
'I become energetic'

[うれしい] → [うれしく] + なります
   い-adjective     く form
            ↓
'I become happy'

の versus と: ロックを聴くのが好きです。 — I like listening to rock; 聴くの makes the action noun-like. ロックを聴くと、いい気分になります。 — When I listen to rock, I feel good; 聴くと introduces a condition.

好き is a な-adjective. これは一番好きな本です。 — This is my favourite book. これが好きです — I like this. Use 好きな before a noun; it isn't これを好き.

Topics and objects: 土曜日は写真を撮ります。（どようびはしゃしんをとります。） — I take photographs on Saturdays. は introduces the topic; を marks the object of 撮る. 友達に電話します — I phone a friend (recipient に). 友達に会います — I meet a friend. 友達を見ます — I see/look at a friend (visually).

Verb contrast: 起きる（おきる） = wake up; 寝る（ねる） = go to bed/sleep; 眠る（ねむる） = sleep. 終わる（おわる） = finish/end; 終わると = when it ends; 終わって = finishes and then...; 終わったあとで = after it has finished.

〜ています can mean an action in progress OR a regular habit. 毎晩本を読んでいます is perfectly reasonable for an established habit; 今本を読んでいます means 'I'm reading now'.

sections.title: While, regrets, wants, must and maybe

parts.text:
〜ながら = while doing: 調べながら読んでいます。（しらべながらよんでいます。） — I'm reading while looking things up.
〜ので = because: 調べながら読んでいるので、返信に時間がかかります。 — Because I read while looking things up, replying takes time.
〜てしまう can express an undesired result OR completion: 返信に時間がかかってしまいます — It ends up taking a while to reply (apologetic). しまいます is non-past polite; しまいました is past.
〜てよかった = I'm glad I did it: 話しかけてよかったです — I'm glad I approached you. 勇気を出してよかったです — I'm glad I found the courage.
〜たい / 〜たかった = want / wanted: 公園に行きたかったけど、雨が降っていました — I wanted to go to the park, but it was raining.
〜なければなりません = have to: 友達に電話しなければなりません. Casual shortened 〜なきゃ: 友達に電話しなきゃ — I have to call my friend.
〜かもしれません = might: 明日は雪が降るかもしれません — It might snow tomorrow.
〜てもいいですか = May I...? ここに座ってもいいですか — May I sit here?

すごく = really/very; 少し（すこし）= a little. すごく勉強になります = 'I'm learning a lot from this / this is really informative', not 'I'm starting to study'.

parts.text:
Translate ONE sentence at a time, without looking at the answer. Request a single-word or single-particle hint only if needed. No repeated "shall we stop?" questions. Reuse patterns, but don't stay on one structure too long.

Round A · everyday Japanese
1. I think this is a good café.
2. When I get home, I listen to music.
3. After I eat breakfast, I read a book.
4. I wanted to go out, but it was raining.
5. I'm glad I tried.
6. It might rain tomorrow.
7. I like taking photos.
8. I don't have time today.

Round B · different meanings
1. My daughter likes writing kanji.
2. I was nervous, but I'm glad I spoke.
3. When I study Japanese, I take notes.
4. I think the park is beautiful.
5. Please wait a little.
6. I have to phone a friend.
7. I'm getting used to speaking Japanese.
8. I wanted tea, but there wasn't any.

Round C · choose your connector
1. I think the teacher is kind. (quoted と)
2. Whenever it rains, I read at home. (conditional と)
3. I like listening to music. (の, not と)
4. After listening to music, I go to bed. (〜たあとで)
5. I listened to music and relaxed. (て-form)
6. I think it might snow. (かもしれない + quotation と)

sections.title: How to continue this practice naturally

parts.text:
Learner preference: practise Japanese by translating varied, short English sentences one at a time. Short, genuine feedback; avoid giving away the complete answer unless asked. The learner sometimes requests a single clue such as just a verb or one particle. Speak Japanese about half the speed of English, with deliberate pauses; English explanations should remain at normal speed. In written examples include kanji with hiragana readings or, when requested, full hiragana, never romaji. Advance to the next prompt after the learner finishes; don't repeatedly ask whether to stop.

Areas to vary: two と structures ('when' vs quotation 'that'), noun/な-adjective + だ, て versus たあとで, 〜のが好き, changes with 〜になる, 〜てよかった, 〜ながら and 〜てしまう, requests, 〜たい / 〜たかった, obligations 〜なきゃ / 〜なければなりません, possibility かもしれません, tense and particles. Keep Japanese natural; accept correct casual and polite forms. If the learner gives よむ instead of よみます, it's a valid plain form, not an error; explain register only when it matters. If the learner says 〜ています for a habit, it can be correct. Correct earlier oversimplifications rather than treating them as target phrases.

sections.title: Words and sentence chunks from speaking practice

parts.text:
Everyday verbs (kanji + reading)
起きる（おきる） wake up; 寝る（ねる） go to bed / sleep; 眠る（ねむる） sleep; 終わる（おわる） finish; 帰る（かえる） return home; 行く（いく） go; 見る（みる） watch/see; 聴く（きく） listen; 聞く（きく） hear/ask; 読む（よむ） read; 書く（かく） write; 撮る（とる） take photos; メモを取る（めもをとる） take notes; 探す（さがす） search for; 払う（はらう） pay; 忘れる（わすれる） forget; 挨拶する（あいさつする） greet; 調べる（しらべる） look up/check; のんびりする relax/take it easy; くつろぐ unwind; 電話する（でんわする） call by phone; 慣れる（なれる） get used to.

Everyday words
日曜日（にちようび） Sunday; 土曜日（どようび） Saturday; 昨日（きのう） yesterday; 明日（あした） tomorrow; 公園（こうえん） park; 学校（がっこう） school; 駅（えき） station; スーパー supermarket; コンビニ convenience store; お茶（おちゃ） tea; お酒（おさけ） alcohol; 傘（かさ） umbrella; 看護師（かんごし） nurse; 友達（ともだち） friend; 返信（へんしん） reply; 時間（じかん） time; 経験（けいけん） experience; 気分（きぶん） mood; 元気（げんき） well/energetic; 悲しい（かなしい） sad; 難しい（むずかしい） difficult; 簡単（かんたん） easy/simple; すごく very/really; 少し（すこし） a little; 気分がいい（きぶんがいい） feel good; しみじみ deeply/reflectively.

Sentence chunks — recall them whole
〜だと思います = I think that [noun / な-adjective]; 〜と、〜になります = when something happens, something becomes; 〜のが好きです = I like doing; 〜たあとで = after doing; 〜て、〜ます = do and then; 〜てよかったです = glad I did; 〜ながら = while doing; 〜てしまいます = end up doing (regret or completion); 〜なければなりません = must; 〜なきゃ = gotta (casual); 〜かもしれません = might; 〜てもいいですか = may I; 〜たいです / 〜たかったです = want to / wanted to; 〜ので = because; けど = but. Read examples in the Grammar and Flashcards views before trying these as free-standing chunks.
